We have with us today Mr. Saugata Basuray, Managing Director, Castrol India Limited; and Ms. 
Mrinalini Srinivasan, Chief Financial Officer, Castrol India Limited. I now hand the conference over 
to Mr. Basuray for his opening remarks. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Saugata Basuray: 
Thank you, and good afternoon, and Namaskar to everyone. Thank you for joining Castrol India's 
analyst call for the third quarter and 9 months ended 30th September 2026. As a reminder, we follow 
the calendar year for financial reporting. I'm joined today by my colleague, Mrinalini Srinivasan, our 
Chief Financial Officer and Whole-Time Director. 
 
In a quarter marked by a sharp rise in raw material costs and adverse currency movements, we 
delivered a resilient performance with revenue up 27% year-on-year. While third quarter profits were 
down 23% year-on-year. Over the 9 months revenue has grown by 20% to INR 5,151 crores. 
EBITDA is up by 11% and profit after tax has risen by 9%. As we flagged in our last call, the increase 
in input costs flowed through in the third quarter. 
 
The pricing actions that we took early in the year in anticipation of the raw material inflation helped 
moderate the impact on margins, and we have held market share across categories. I would add that 
our business should not be read sequentially as the second quarter is traditionally our strongest 
quarter, driven by seasonal demand from agriculture and associated movement of goods, which we 
catch up in the freight and commercial vehicle business. 
 
We are focused on recovering margins and investing in our growth engines. Even as we manage near-
term cost pressures, we kept investing in our infrastructure in rural India, building out the industrial 
business, which delivered another quarter of double-digit volume growth. 
 
So let me just highlight 5 areas that define our quarter. The first is about distribution reach. We 
expanded our national footprint to approximately 167,000 outlets, including 46,000 of those outlets, 
which are in rural small town India. Auto Care, which is an adjacent business that we introduced a 
few years back is now available across 50,000 physical stores, is doing very well on e-commerce and 
modern trade.

Our service ecosystem now includes about 870 Castrol Auto Service centers, 37,000 independent 
bike workshops and 16,000 multi-brand workshops. While our Rural Service Express has expanded 
to over 1,000 locations. 
 
Customer growth in the industrial business has been strong. This business continues to grow double 
digits. In the full year and9 months that has followed, we have added close to 400 customers net, and 
that helped us generate new business as well as drive the top line growth. 
 
We have also launched Magna CTX, a range of circulating oils designed for demanding industrial 
lubricant applications. We have also localized a lot of our products, and this is in pursuit of getting 
better control on our raw material costs. We have brought along new products such as Hysol 35 XBB, 
and Hysol 61 XBB, boron-free metalworking fluids which is designed for industrial machines. 
 
On the brand side, we strengthened Castrol MAGNATEC proposition of non-stop protection even 
before you start, highlighting how the molecules inside this product protect critical engine parts. 
Meanwhile, our "Freedom to Ride" community program for bikers continues to move across cities: 
Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad in the quarter that went by. 
 
Our Super Mechanics program celebrates the graduation-day of mechanics who have received 
certification and training. They've been certified by ASDC, India's first sector skill council for the 
automotive industry. Fast Scan platform has now got verified mechanics, mechanics who have 
confirmed their identity to Castrol, which is up almost 100,000 to 180,000, which is 24% more than 
last year at the same time. 
 
We showcase our industrial lubricants business and our heavy-duty solutions across various 
platforms, such as CONEXPO and bauma, alongside large machine tool and industrial exhibition 
customers. 
 
We also had some accolades in this particular quarter. Noteworthy on them was a ET Brand Equity 
Award. We were also ranked in the top 10 Supply Chain Planning Champions and placed seventh in 
Supply Chain Excellence by the Institute of Supply Chain Management. Our Silvassa and Paharpur 
facilities won Gold at the regional chapter of the Convention of Quality Concepts, recognizing 
improvements in operational efficiency and manufacturing. 
 
These actions reinforce our strategy, premiumize the portfolio, go deep in distribution, urban and 
rural markets, build a strong service ecosystem and prepare for the future of mobility. We continue 
to see meaningful headroom for growth in rural India. And our long-term ambition is to evolve from 
a lubricants company into a broader mobility solutions and maintenance partner. 
 
Our industrial business is a growing part of the story. Its double-digit volume growth this quarter, 
together with new customer addition across sectors, reflects the strength of our technical expertise, 
our advanced solutions and the trust of customers placed on us.

approximately 15% for the quarter. Profit after tax was INR176 crores, down 23% year-on-year and 
49% sequentially.

was INR5,151 crores, up 20% year-on-year. EBITDA was INR1,086 crores, up 11% year-on-year, 
supported by the pricing action we took early on in the year. EBITDA margin of approximately 21% 
for the 9 months period. Profit before tax was INR1,043 crores, up 10% and profit after tax was 
INR766 crores, up 9%. 
 
Revenue growth in the quarter was supported by the pricing actions we took early in the year. 
Sequentially, our performance is lower largely because of seasonality and timing. As Saugata 
mentioned, the second quarter is traditionally our strongest, driven by seasonal demand from agri. In 
addition, as we said on our last call, cost escalations flow through to the P&L with a little bit of a lag, 
and we expected some of those to land in this third quarter. Increases in commodity and input costs, 
along with the broader inflationary pressures began flowing in towards the end of second quarter and 
became more visible in the third with high double-digit commodity inflation. 
 
Adverse currency movements added further pressure. Pricing helped moderate this impact, and we 
held market leadership, while we continue to invest in the levers as Saugata mentioned, rural 
distribution and industrial business of our brands.

and will make percentage margins appear softer for some time. While unit profitability margin 
remains intact. In this time of extreme volatility, for us, margin per liter is a true measure. And on 
that basis, we have fully absorbed cost inflation. Margins are steady to slightly higher. Protecting 
margins per liter will remain our priority.

industrial continue to grow, and we expect these to grow ahead of the market. We will continue to 
monitor input costs, currency, pricing and demand closely and act with agility to manage margin 
pressure in the medium term. Our focus remains on recovering margins, disciplined execution, 
careful cost management, resilient supply and sustained investment in the long-term competitiveness.
